description: Two channels turning a 0V to 10V control voltage into the loudness of one shared high sine carrier, so the voltage can travel down an audio cable

params.text: Sets the level of the carrier both channels use, 0 to 1; at 1 a 10V input gives a carrier swinging 9.99V either side of zero, and at 0 both outputs are silent

inputs.text: The control voltage for that channel; it is divided by 10 and clamped to 0 and 1, so anything at or below 0V silences that output and anything from 10V up holds the carrier at full level

outputs.text: The carrier scaled by the voltage at IN 1, a sine at 8697.36Hz
The carrier scaled by the voltage at IN 2, a sine at 8697.36Hz, despite the maker's tooltip on this jack reading OUT 1

notes: With nothing patched into a channel's IN jack, that channel's OUT jack carries the bare carrier at whatever the CARRIER knob is set to, rather than silence.
The red lamp beside an input lights for negative voltage there, brightening from 0V down to -10V, despite its tooltip naming it a warning for signals above +10V.
Both channels take the same carrier oscillator, so the two outputs are always in phase.
The module has no menu of its own beyond Rack's.
